notes:
I don't have any commentary notes for you on Isaiah 30. My first attempt to fetch the sources crashed because of a bug in my own code. Before I could rerun it, I hit the limit on tool calls for this turn. I didn't read a single page, so I have nothing sourced to report.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. Writing verse-by-verse notes from memory and attaching URLs would break that rule, so I've left the notes out entirely.

**What I'll do when you ask again (e.g. "continue"):**

1. **Verse-by-verse traditional reading**, from:
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-30/
   - preceptaustin.org's Isaiah 30 commentary page
   - biblehub.com's Isaiah 30 pages for Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Matthew Henry
2. **Places where Protestant traditions differ**, from each tradition's own teachers. Likely candidates:
   - v. 15, "repentance and rest… quiet confidence": what faith and rest mean, and how they relate to repentance
   - v. 18, "the LORD longs to be gracious"
   - vv. 20–21, the "Teacher" and the voice saying "This is the way": whether the Teacher is God, Christ, human teachers or the Spirit's guidance today
   - v. 33, Topheth and judgment
   - Sources: Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon sermons, Ligonier/TGC/Desiring God articles, and Lutheran material on lcms.org and 1517.org
3. **Other views, only where well known:**
   - netbible.org notes, especially on "Rahab Who Sits Still" (v. 7), Zoan and Hanes (v. 4), and Topheth (v. 33)
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org)
   - Popular modern teaching on vv. 21 or 23: I'll include it only if those sites actually discuss it.

I'll leave out any verse where I can't find a sourced comment.
